fact: ARCT acting director Hermalas Nahimana said the government has created a universal service fund that will help the rural population to have access to the internet.

SETIC (also PAFEN coordinator) signed a $5,907,000 contract with ONATEL to deploy infrastructure across 92 rural hills lacking 2G or 3G coverage, expected to benefit about 372,035 people, said Burundi Times.

PAFEN, the government digital-inclusion programme, and Lumitel signed a USD 10 million contract to extend 4G broadband in rural areas, co-financed 44 per cent by the government through PAFEN, says SETIC.

Burundi's Universal Service Fund (FSU-TIC) revised FY2025/26 procurement plan funds 3 pilot Villages Numeriques in the provinces of Bujumbura, Gitega and Buhumuza at BIF 4,811,751,000, per the fund's own plan.
